verses.text: This is what the LORD says: "Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and announce this message there:
'Listen to the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne, you and your officials and your people who come through these gates.

This is what the LORD says: Do what is fair and right. Rescue the person who has been robbed from the one who treats them cruelly. Do not mistreat or harm the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow. Do not kill innocent people in this place.
For if you truly obey these commands, then kings who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, with their officials and their people.
But if you do not obey these words, I promise by my own name, says the LORD, that this palace will become a ruin.'"
For this is what the LORD says about the palace of the king of Judah: "You are like Gilead to me, like the top of Lebanon. But I will surely make you like a wilderness, like towns where no one lives.
I will send destroyers against you, each with his weapons. They will cut down your finest cedar beams and throw them into the fire.
People from many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?'
And the answer will be, 'Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God. They worshiped and served other gods.'"
Do not weep for the dead king or mourn for him. Instead, weep bitterly for the one who is being taken away, for he will never come back to see his homeland again.
For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, who became king of Judah after his father but has left this place: "He will never come back.
He will die in the place where they have taken him as a captive. He will never see this land again."
"How terrible for the king who builds his palace by doing wrong, and its upper rooms by injustice, who makes his own people work for nothing and does not pay them for their work!
He says, 'I will build myself a great palace with large upper rooms.' He cuts out windows for it, covers it with cedar, and paints it red.
Does having more cedar make you a king? Your father had enough to eat and drink. He did what was fair and right, so everything went well for him.
He defended the cause of the poor and needy, so everything went well. Is that not what it means to know me?" says the LORD.
"But your eyes and your heart are set only on dishonest gain, on killing innocent people, and on cruelty and violence."

So this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: "People will not mourn for him, saying, 'Oh, my brother! Oh, my sister!' They will not mourn for him, saying, 'Oh, my master! Oh, his glory!'
He will be buried like a dead donkey, dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem."
"Go up to Lebanon and cry out. Let your voice be heard in Bashan. Cry out from Abarim, for all your allies have been crushed.
I warned you when you felt safe, but you said, 'I will not listen!' This has been your way since you were young. You have never obeyed me.
The wind will drive all your leaders away, and your allies will go into exile. Then you will be ashamed and disgraced because of all your wickedness.
You who live in Lebanon, who nest among the cedars, how you will groan when pain comes on you, pain like a woman giving birth!
As surely as I live," says the LORD, "even if you, Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would still pull you off.
I will hand you over to those who want to kill you, those you are afraid of, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Babylonians.
I will throw you and the mother who gave birth to you into another country, where neither of you was born, and there you will both die.
You will never come back to the land you long to return to."
Is this man Coniah a hated, broken pot, something no one wants? Why will he and his children be thrown out and sent to a land they do not know?
O land, land, land, listen to the word of the LORD!

This is what the LORD says: "Write this man down as if he had no children, a man who will not succeed in his lifetime. None of his descendants will succeed in sitting on David's throne or ruling in Judah again."
